# Dr Xiaoxiong Xie

::: {.position}
Lecturer in Building Engineering\
University of Plymouth, UK
:::

::: {.summary}
My research focuses on **urban–building climate interactions**: how local climate affects building energy demand and thermal conditions, and how buildings change their surroundings.

I use coupled **SUEWS–EnergyPlus modelling** to study these feedbacks, alongside collaborative work on environmental monitoring. Applications include natural ventilation, heat pumps and climate-resilient retrofit.
:::

[Explore my research →](research/index.qmd){.text-link}

[Methods and supporting publications](research/index.qmd#methods-and-evidence)
:::

::: {.hero-aside}

Building engineering and urban climatology, with a focus on the places where people live and the systems that heat and cool them.

## Three connected research themes

::: {.theme-grid}
::: {.theme}
[01]{.number}

### Buildings in their urban context

How do local temperature, wind and radiation change the performance of buildings—and how do buildings change their surroundings?

[Urban–building interactions](research/index.qmd#urban-building-interactions)
:::
::: {.theme}
[02]{.number}

### Thermal resilience & retrofit

How can retrofit and natural ventilation reduce energy demand while responding to overheating and future climate conditions?

[Climate-resilient buildings](research/index.qmd#climate-resilient-retrofit)
:::
::: {.theme}
[03]{.number}

### Low-carbon energy & thermal exposure

How do changing heating and cooling systems affect urban environments, and how can monitoring help us understand those environments?

[Energy systems and exposure](research/index.qmd#low-carbon-technologies)
:::
:::

::: {}
[Research explainer]{.eyebrow}

## How do air-source heat pumps affect urban microclimates?

A closer look at the exchange of heat between homes and neighbourhoods, using coupled urban climate and building energy simulations.

[Read the explainer →](research/heat-pumps/index.qmd){.text-link}
:::
::: {.feature-note}
**From building performance to local climate**

Based on our 2024 paper in *Sustainable Cities and Society*. The research uses future climate scenarios; its temperature changes are modelled outcomes.

[Original publication](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scs.2024.105811)
:::
:::

## Selected research contributions

::: {.contribution-list}
- **Connecting scales:** SUEWS–EnergyPlus studies of [natural ventilation](publications/index.qmd#xie-2023-density) and [heat-pump interactions with urban climate](publications/index.qmd#xie-2024-heat-pumps).
- **Placing retrofit in context:** Principal Investigator of [UMAR](projects/index.qmd#umar), a project on microclimate-aware retrofit that ran from October 2025 to September 2026.
- **Understanding outdoor conditions:** Collaborative work on [mobile environmental monitoring](publications/index.qmd#lam-2025-monitoring) and [crowdsourced temperature data](publications/index.qmd#he-2025-gap-filling).
:::
